conversations.topic: Jeans and clothing purchase with discount negotiation

speakers.speaker: A (salesperson)
speakers.summary: Mostly polite, helpful, and composed. Shows brief unease when the customer threatens cancellation and momentary stress when calling for assistance, then returns to calmly handling the discount request.

speakers.speaker: B (customer)
speakers.summary: Initially neutral, with intermittent humor and cooperation. Complains about color availability and changing-room cleanliness, then becomes more irritated after the salesperson's sizing suggestion, threatens cancellation, and complains about treatment. Later agrees to buy but remains impatient and demanding about the discount; the final acknowledgment is neutral.

speakers.speaker: @ (other)
speakers.summary: Only a brief, calm acknowledgment is available; there is no evidence of frustration.

frustration_moments.evidence: Repeated imperative and insistence on a higher discount indicate impatience in context. The voice is labeled demanding and firm, with elevated loudness and pitch providing supporting evidence.

customer_requested: Louis Vuitton slim-fit jeans, size 36, rather than Levi's.
Brown jeans initially, then blue jeans.
A light-colored, full-sleeve shirt after accepting the matching-shirt suggestion.
Underwear ('jokey jokey') to cover the remaining 400 rupees toward the discount threshold.

upsell_attempts.quote: Yes, I can show you a shirt also with that matching shirt
upsell_attempts.offered_item: A matching shirt to accompany the jeans

upsell_attempts.quote: but you are still uh won't be able to get the 20 percent discount would you do would you like to have belts
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Belts to help qualify for the 20% discount

So would you like to try this? -> Offers a fitting of the requested jeans, not an additional purchase.

Yes, sir. It is elastic. What size you would... Oh, for you, I think S is the enough. -> A sizing suggestion for requested underwear, not an upsell.

you take one free offer if you take one more jean we will give you one thing which is free of cost there. -> Spoken by the customer, not the salesperson, so it is not counted as a salesperson's bundle offer.
upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer said 'I'm canceling my order' and complained about 'the way you're talking to me,' the salesperson warned that the 20% discount would be lost and suggested belts instead of first resolving the customer's frustration.
upsell.summary: There were three upsell attempts: a spending-threshold discount, a matching shirt, and belts. The customer initially rejected spending 5000 but accepted the shirt suggestion; the later belt pitch received no clear answer and came while the customer was frustrated.
upsell.greeting_quote: Hello, sir. How can I help you?
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer complained that there was no brown color, the dress room was 'very dirty,' and, after the sizing suggestion, objected to 'the way you're talking to me.'
upsell.coaching_feedback: Your 'Hello, sir. How can I help you?' opener was welcoming, and the matching-shirt suggestion earned an explicit 'that's a good idea.' After 'I'm canceling my order' and the complaint about how you were speaking, pause the add-on pitch, apologize for the sizing remark, and confirm what the customer still wants before suggesting belts or emphasizing the discount threshold.
